Reason: The CT images demonstrate a right pleural effusion and an anomalous vessel draining into the inferior vena cava/right atrium region (scimitar vein), which corresponds to the "left second arc protrusion" (likely referring to the prominent right heart border/scimitar sign often mislabeled or describing the vascular anomaly's projection) seen on chest X-ray. This constellation of findings in an elderly patient with dyspnea is characteristic of Scimitar syndrome (a congenital vascular anomaly), distinguishing it from common causes like heart failure or pneumonia.
